rhs_for_integrator: mu0 * n * A * dIdt / (1 + (mu0 * n * A * dIdt / emf_sat)**2) * (1 + eddy_coeff * mu0 * n * A * dIdt * tanh(mu0 * n * A * dIdt / emf_eddy)) * (1 + eddy_temp_coeff * (T - T_ref)) / (1 + skin_coeff * (f_drive * sqrt(1 + (mu0 * n * A * dIdt / emf_eddy)**2))**(sigma_skin) * (1 + skin_temp_coeff * (T - T_ref))) * (1 - hyst_coeff * exp(-emf_sat / (mu0 * n * A * Abs(dIdt) + emf_hyst)))
sanity_expectations: emf is finite, real and positive over the whole sampled region
emf is non-monotonic in dIdt: rises to a peak near dIdt~2e4 (drive ~ emf_sat) then declines at high dIdt due to the 1/(1+(drive/emf_sat)^2) saturation factor
emf increases weakly and monotonically with temperature T (eddy_temp_coeff numerator gain outweighs skin_temp_coeff denominator loss)
the hysteresis factor reduces emf most at high drive (large dIdt), shaving up to ~hyst_coeff (~30%) off the parent value; negligible correction at low dIdt
at fixed T the response is smooth with no discontinuities
excitation_report: Noise yardstick sigma=0.002 (abs std on emf; ~1.5% of peak emf ~0.14). k=5. Single top-level product term: rms 0.101 = 50.5*sigma (dominant, visible). NEW term (hysteresis factor 1 - hyst_coeff*exp(-emf_sat/(mu0*n*A*|dIdt|+emf_hyst))): max_effect 0.0268 = 13.4*sigma, strongest at dIdt~4.95e4, T~371 (high-drive regime where exp arg -> 0 so the deficit saturates to ~hyst_coeff). All terms visible; no weak terms.
role_corrections: dIdt: V->independent variable, primary sampling axis (confirmed)
T: V->independent variable, second axis via eddy/skin temperature factors (confirmed)
n: V->P (overridden: enters ONLY through product mu0*n*A*dIdt, degenerate with dIdt; fixed as geometry constant)
A: V->P (overridden: same product degeneracy as n; fixed as geometry constant)
rationale: The expression is an explicit closed form for emf with no derivatives or integral kernels (analyze_expression: max_derivative_order=0, no integral_kernels, explicitly_solvable_for_target=true) -> equation_type=explicit, integrator=evaluate_explicit. Roles: emf is the LHS output; dIdt and T are the genuine sampling axes (dIdt is the physical variable recorded 'for different rates of current change'; T modulates via the eddy/skin temperature factors). n and A are demoted from the pipeline's 'input' label to fixed parameters because they appear exclusively inside the product mu0*n*A*dIdt and are structurally indistinguishable from dIdt, so sampling them would only add rank-deficient columns; they are fixed at physical solenoid values (n=5000 turns/m, A=2e-3 m^2). Parameter magnitudes chosen so the flux drive mu0*n*A*dIdt sweeps ~1.3e-3 to ~1.26 V across the dIdt range, straddling emf_sat=emf_eddy=0.3 so the saturation, eddy-reinforcement, skin and hysteresis factors are all exercised. Suggested hint ranges honored (hyst_coeff=0.3 in [0.01,0.5], emf_hyst=0.01 in [1e-4,1e-1]). check_substitution at a mid point gave emf=0.136 (finite, real). excitation_check confirms all terms and the new hysteresis term exceed 5*sigma, so excitation_ok=true.

scenario_text: A long solenoid carries a steadily increasing current, and the changing magnetic flux inside induces an electric field that opposes the flux growth. We record the magnitude of the induced electromotive force around a coaxial loop for different rates of current change. The number of turns and coil geometry set the coupling. Each configuration yields an instantaneous induced voltage.
